A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoR framework, MPM dataset, and Progressive Paradigm Training strategy. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison; material moved between the main text and appendices was matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original CoR evaluations on five mathematical benchmarks, training-stage and paradigm-order ablations, model-scaling experiments, and additional appendix analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds single-paradigm fine-tuning comparisons, sampled-error analysis, and generated reasoning cases.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction procedure, three-stage PPT training, likelihood objective, paradigm chaining, and SMPS inference remain unchanged. The new instruction-free cases document behavior of the existing model rather than introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Training sources and all five evaluation benchmarks are retained. Appendix D.1 adds a qualitative arithmetic scenario without explicit paradigm-switching instructions, extending the demonstrated input conditions. The added AMC2023 and AIME2024 dataset-statistics rows describe benchmarks already evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: V3 Table 5 adds NLR-only, AR-only, and SR-only fine-tuned DeepSeekMath controls against CoR. The external comparator sets in the corresponding main benchmark tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6.4 introduces an ablation reporting identical backbones, problem sets, and 10,000 training samples per paradigm. Appendix D.2 specifies random samples of 200 arithmetic and 50 theorem-proving errors. Table 1 also changes GPT-4's AMC2023 and AIME2024 annotations from the default few-shot setting to zero-shot, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained stage, order, scaling, leakage, and majority-voting analyses, v3 adds a direct single-versus-multiple-paradigm training comparison in Section 6.4. Appendix D substantially expands diagnostic analysis through error categorization, instruction-free reasoning, proof failures, and self-correction cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The newly reported error-category frequencies are descriptive results rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V3 adds quantitative findings about single-paradigm training and failure distributions. Table 5 newly reports MATH scores of 27.8 for NLR-only and 37.6 for AR-only training alongside CoR's 66.7; Appendix D.2 reports incomplete-proof/syntax errors in 85 of 200 arithmetic errors and 33 of 50 theorem-proving errors. Table 1 revises Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct from 10/40 to 16/40 on AMC2023 and from 0/30 to 5/30 on AIME2024, matching v2's prose. Existing headline CoR scores are retained.

T1.justification: The conditional-generation equations, training loss, SMPS formulation, and sample-budget definitions are unchanged. The reasoning-hierarchy discussion is relocated, and the added proof/code outputs are empirical cases rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: Both versions claim unified NLR/AR/SR reasoning, progressive paradigm training, zero-shot mathematical generalization, and improved resource efficiency. The abstract retains the same headline performance claims. New analyses support these existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V3 adds explicit limitations concerning alignment of zero-shot/few-shot evaluations and restricted SMPS evaluation on arithmetic benchmarks. Appendix D.2 adds explanations involving scarce SR pretraining data, context-window truncation, and complementary cross-paradigm correction. The earlier hierarchy and synergy discussion remains in Appendix A.

D1.justification: V3 adds a CoR code-repository pointer in the abstract and completes dataset statistics for AMC2023 and AIME2024. It removes the explicit miniF2F Lean4-port URL supplied in v2. The documented learning rate, warm-up, epochs, sequence lengths, optimization tools, and annealing strategy are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds five cited works, including Critical Tokens Matter, URSA, Data Whisperer, SSR, and Zhao and Zhang's compositional-reasoning study. Section 3.3 also distinguishes PPT from curriculum and incremental learning. The principal positioning against single-paradigm and tool-interleaved reasoning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Existing prose is extensively condensed and rewritten across the introduction, related work, methodology, and results. Ablations become a separate Section 6, while v2's Section 6 moves to Appendix A. V3 also adds dedicated limitations and case-study sections and updates author information.

P2.justification: V3 changes the document from one to two columns, rearranges Figures 1, 5, and 6, and substantially restyles and relocates tables and captions. It adds Table 5 and Figures 10–12. Figure 1 additionally plots two DeepSeekMath models whose scores were already tabulated in v2; Table 4 reverses its paradigm-order columns without changing results.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful evidence about paradigm combinations and failure modes, states evaluation limitations, and resolves Table 1's disagreement with the Llama scores in the prose. These improve support and transparency around the retained method. The gain is limited by defects in the additions: Figure 12 contains an unrelated Lean output of 27.000000, and Table 1's caption reverses the counts of model categories and benchmarks. Overall, the diagnostic additions support a modest net improvement.
